math_plain: Uses learned semantic alignment to rank and assign product types to campaigns based on content interpretation.
why_math: It works because campaigns have consistent thematic intent; grounding that intent against the product taxonomy maps ambiguous language to concrete purchase patterns, so the model learns real causal structure from aligned labels.

math_tags: combining many weak signals into a strong one
math_plain: A single model learns to generate task-specific agent collaboration graphs by dynamically selecting relevant expert sub-networks based on task description.
why_math: It works because different task types exhibit recurring structural patterns; by separating the task-aware selection from base graph prediction, the model captures what collaboration patterns work for different problem classes without overfitting to single tasks.

math_plain: Federated clients cluster their graphs locally while decoupling public shared structure from private local patterns to align clusters despite mismatched cluster counts.
why_math: It works because real cluster structure is partially shared and partially domain-specific; by modeling both explicitly and only aggregating the public side, each client remains aligned without forcing false consensus on granularity.

math_tags: ranking things by a learned score
math_plain: A lightweight pre-trained classifier learns to rank and localize rumor sources by scoring subgraph regions, then adapts via prompting rather than full retraining.
why_math: It works because source localization is fundamentally about identifying which parts of the network exhibit source-like behavior; pre-training on synthetic diffusion data with prompting adaptation avoids re-running expensive simulations for each new outbreak.

math_tags: combining many weak signals into a strong one
math_plain: A federated forecaster decomposes time-series into global low-frequency shared patterns and client-specific high-frequency patterns, then recombines them for prediction.
why_math: It works because real time-series have universal rhythms shared across clients and unique local variations; by splitting these and handling them separately before fusion, the model captures what generalizes across domains without forcing clients to agree on all details.

math_tags: measuring similarity as nearness in a space
math_plain: Represents users and items on an adaptive curved manifold where the local geometry adjusts to match graph topology, enabling similarity to be measured as shortest path distance.
why_math: It works because real user-item graphs have varying density and structure; by letting the geometric space bend to fit the actual topology rather than forcing flat-space assumptions, distances in the manifold capture true behavioral similarity.

weighting the parts that are most relevant
math_plain: A cross-level mechanism first grounds text descriptions in visual context, then uses those descriptions to focus the visual encoder on anomalous regions.
why_math: It works because fine-grained defects require top-down linguistic guidance combined with bottom-up visual focus; by enforcing sequential alignment where vision informs text and text refocuses vision, the model grounds semantics in diagnostic reality rather than treating modalities independently.

math_plain: An LLM learns graph-to-text alignment by reconstructing graph structure from its internal token outputs, adding explicit graph supervision to language-only instruction tuning.
why_math: It works because text-only supervision creates asymmetry where language dominates and graph context is underutilized; by requiring reconstruction of the original graph, you force the model to preserve all information, making alignment bidirectional rather than text-biased.

math_plain: Combines a ranking model's scores with a probability sample of documents to estimate true recall without judging the entire corpus, enabling early stopping decisions.
why_math: It works because the ranker's scores act as an informative prior about which documents are likely relevant; updating that prior with random samples gives unbiased estimates, and confidence bounds tell you when additional sampling won't substantially improve the estimate.

math_tags: measuring similarity as nearness in a space
math_plain: Dynamically extracts query-relevant subgraphs by finding attributed communities that match the question, then passes these self-complementary subgraphs to the LLM.
why_math: It works because knowledge bases have natural clusters of related facts; retrieving an entire community around query-relevant nodes captures implicit context and connections that single-node or low-order retrieval would miss, enriching the LLM's grounding.

math_tags: matching and allocating who gets what
math_plain: Determines fair prices for data by balancing supply and demand while allowing each data record to be sold to multiple buyers simultaneously.
why_math: It works because data is non-rival but does degrade predictive performance when shared; equilibrium prices reflect both intrinsic scarcity and the marginal value each buyer extracts, settling at a price where no buyer or seller wants to deviate.

math_tags: combining many weak signals into a strong one
math_plain: A gated mixture model decomposes deepfakes into semantic content variations and forgery technique artifacts, learning separate branches for each to improve generalization.
why_math: It works because deepfakes from different techniques have distinct failure modes; treating all fakes identically obscures these patterns, but disentangling technique-specific artifacts allows the model to learn what actually distinguishes real from fake within each generation method.

math_tags: keeping only the few dimensions that matter
math_plain: Analyzes pointer patterns to partition memory into isolated regions, then rewrites the binary to map each region to separate memory instances without adding runtime checks.
why_math: It works because memory safety violations depend on spatial locality; by enforcing boundaries only where they matter (region transitions), you prevent exploits while avoiding the cost of checking every access.

math_tags: predicting the next item in a sequence
math_plain: Uses conditional probability of power load given the past 60 seconds of history to predict upcoming battery demand and reduce uncertainty.
why_math: It works because driver behavior is partially predictable within short windows; conditioning on recent history removes noise from one-shot predictions and captures momentum in usage patterns, revealing true upcoming load better than static averages.

math_tags: learning by comparison of similar and different
math_plain: Mines category-specific behavior patterns from sequences and contextualizes action semantics to distinguish illicit from benign accounts even when actions look identical.
why_math: It works because illicit actors follow regularities like benign users, but patterns differ; by extracting behavior sequences rather than profiles and adjusting action meaning by context, the model captures that the same action serves different purposes under different conditions.
